close_reason: Added PartialEq behavior warning to TrustAnchor rustdoc: explains byte-level comparison and directs users to names_match + key-bytes comparison for deduplication
description: TrustAnchor derives PartialEq, which includes SubjectPublicKeyInfoOwned::PartialEq — a field-by-field comparison that treats Some(NULL) != None for algorithm parameters. A user who deduplicates their trust store by comparing TrustAnchor values with == could get false negatives for two anchors representing the same CA but with different parameter encodings. This is the same issue that was just fixed in the validate_path guard. The fix should either: (a) document the footgun on TrustAnchor::PartialEq, or (b) implement a custom PartialEq that uses spki_key_matches logic (would require making spki_key_matches or a variant pub(crate)).
title: TrustAnchor::PartialEq has same NULL-vs-absent footgun as the fixed guard
